summary: Defines an IMAP extension that lets a client ask for specific unsolicited notifications about chosen mailboxes, such as messages being added or deleted. This is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5267.

eli5.summary: Instead of constantly asking if there is new mail, the mail program can ask the server to tell it when something changes.

questions: how to get push notifications from imap
how to watch multiple mailboxes in imap
subtitle: How an IMAP client tells the server exactly which mailbox changes to push, without keeping a connection open per mailbox.

tldr.problem: IMAP IDLE only pushes events for the selected mailbox and gives the client no control over which events or what data arrive, so watching several mailboxes needs an extra TCP connection per mailbox.
tldr.mechanism: The NOTIFY command lets a client list which mailboxes to watch and which events (new messages, expunges, flag changes, renames and more) the server should send unsolicited, even between commands.
tldr.outcome: A client can stay synchronised through one connection and ask for only what it needs, but it must be careful: asking for too much can swamp the client, and the server may refuse with NOTIFICATIONOVERFLOW.

facts.label: Required rights
facts.value: l and r on every observed mailbox

today: RFC 5465 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2009. It updates RFC 5267, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why IDLE Is Not Enough
sections.content:
Without this extension, an IMAP server only tells a client about mailstore changes in three cases: as the result of a client command, as unsolicited responses sent just before the end of a command, and during an IDLE command (RFC 2177).

IDLE has two limits. It does not restrict or control which server events are sent, or what information goes with each one. And it only applies to the selected mailbox, so watching more mailboxes needs an additional TCP connection per mailbox.

The NOTIFY command fixes both. Clients only receive the events they want, and servers know they can skip generating other untagged responses. A client can also be a passive recipient of new mail and stay fully synchronised without issuing further commands except to change mailbox state.
sections.eli5: The old way only let you watch one mailbox at a time and gave you no say in what you were told. This new way lets you pick what to hear about, from many mailboxes, over one line.

sections.title: The NOTIFY Command
sections.content:
Servers that support the extension advertise the NOTIFY capability. The command has two forms: NOTIFY NONE, which says the client is not interested in any events, and NOTIFY SET, which replaces the current list of interesting events with a new list. The effect lasts until the next NOTIFY command or until the connection closes.

Until NOTIFY is used for the first time, the server only sends notifications while a command is being processed, and only about MessageNew, MessageExpunge or FlagChange on the selected mailbox. After a successful NOTIFY SET, the server MUST immediately return any accumulated changes to the selected mailbox, so the command implies a NOOP.

If the client adds the optional STATUS indicator, the server MUST send a STATUS response for each newly watched non-selected mailbox before the tagged OK. Leaving it out avoids those extra responses when the client already knows the numbers.

The server checks access for each named mailbox. A missing mailbox, or one the client cannot LIST, MUST be silently ignored so nothing confidential leaks. A mailbox the client can list but lacks a needed right for gets an extended LIST response with the \NoAccess attribute. If the request is prohibitively expensive, the server MAY refuse with a tagged NO [NOTIFICATIONOVERFLOW]. An unsupported event type MUST get a tagged NO (not BAD), ideally with a BADEVENT code listing the supported events.

Clients are advised to limit the number of mailboxes they watch. Asking for events on every accessible mailbox can swamp the client with updates about shared mailboxes, shorten battery life and waste server and network resources.
sections.eli5: You hand the clerk a list: these mailboxes, these kinds of news. The clerk hands you a quick summary right away, then keeps you posted. If your list is silly-huge, the clerk can say no.

sections.title: Choosing Mailboxes and Events
sections.content:
A NOTIFY SET contains one or more event groups. Each group pairs a mailbox filter with a list of events, or with NONE. Several groups can apply to the same mailbox, so the events add up.

The mailbox filters are:

  • SELECTED and SELECTED-DELAYED: the currently selected mailbox. Only one of the two may appear in a command, and they accept only message events.
  • PERSONAL: all selectable mailboxes in the user's personal namespaces.
  • INBOXES: personal mailboxes that a message delivery agent may deliver to. If the server cannot easily compute this, it MUST treat it as PERSONAL.
  • SUBSCRIBED: all subscribed mailboxes, re-evaluated when the subscription list changes.
  • SUBTREE: the named mailbox or mailboxes plus everything beneath them.
  • MAILBOXES: exactly the named mailboxes, with no wildcard expansion.

For the selected mailbox, SELECTED overrides any other message-event settings, even if the mailbox is also named elsewhere. Omitting a selected group is the same as SELECTED NONE. Keywords are case-insensitive.

The MessageNew event may carry a list of FETCH attributes, but only for the selected mailbox. MessageNew and MessageExpunge MUST always be specified together, and FlagChange or AnnotationChange require both, otherwise the server answers BAD.
sections.eli5: Your list says which mailboxes (the one you are reading, all your own, the ones you subscribed to, a folder and its sub-folders, or ones you name) and what news you want from each.

sections.title: Event Types and How the Server Reports Them
sections.content:
The server SHOULD NOT notify a client about an event the same client caused. All event types need the l and r rights (RFC 4314) on every observed mailbox.

  • MessageNew: in the selected mailbox, an unsolicited EXISTS followed by a FETCH with the requested data. In another mailbox, an unsolicited STATUS (UIDNEXT MESSAGES).
  • MessageExpunge: EXPUNGE, or VANISHED when QRESYNC (RFC 5162) is enabled. In another mailbox, a STATUS response.
  • FlagChange and AnnotationChange: an unsolicited FETCH with UID and the flags or annotation. In another mailbox, a STATUS, which includes HIGHESTMODSEQ and UIDVALIDITY if CONDSTORE or QRESYNC is enabled.
  • MailboxName: an unsolicited LIST for each mailbox created, deleted or renamed. A deleted or inaccessible name carries \NonExistent, and a rename carries an OLDNAME data item.
  • SubscriptionChange: an unsolicited LIST, with \Subscribed if and only if the mailbox is subscribed afterwards.
  • MailboxMetadataChange and ServerMetadataChange: an unsolicited METADATA response (RFC 5464). Support is optional unless the server supports METADATA.

If a search context from RFC 5267 is active, the matching ESEARCH ADDTO or REMOVEFROM response is also generated, after the EXISTS or FETCH response.

Access can change later. If a client loses access to a watched mailbox, the server MUST stop monitoring it and MUST restart monitoring if access is granted again.
sections.eli5: Each kind of news arrives in its own kind of note. News about the mailbox you are reading comes with details. News about other mailboxes is a short update saying how many messages are there now.

sections.title: Working with IDLE and Message Numbers
sections.content:
If both IDLE and NOTIFY are supported, then while any IDLE command runs, the server MUST send exactly the events the client asked for with NOTIFY. For clients that do not use message sequence numbers (MSNs) or the asterisk in commands, NOTIFY makes IDLE unnecessary.

MSNs are a catch. If a client asks for MessageExpunge with plain SELECTED, the meaning of an MSN can change at any time, so the client has to use UID FETCH rather than FETCH. The meaning of the asterisk (the last-message shortcut) can also shift as messages arrive or vanish.

A client that wants to keep using MSNs can pick SELECTED-DELAYED. The server then delays MessageExpunge until the client issues a command that may return expunge information, such as NOOP or IDLE. It MAY also delay other message events.
sections.eli5: If the numbers on the mail in your tray are renumbered every time something is removed, you can get confused. Asking for delayed news means the renumbering waits until you say you are ready.

sections.title: Pushing New Search Matches
sections.content:
This RFC updates RFC 5267. When a server supports NOTIFY and also CONTEXT=SEARCH or CONTEXT=SORT, the UPDATE return option can carry a list of FETCH attributes. Then, when a new message joins the context result set, the server sends those attributes along.

The order is fixed: EXISTS MUST precede any FETCH, and together they MUST precede the ESEARCH response. If the NOTIFY command and the search both ask for attributes of a new message, the server SHOULD combine them into one FETCH and avoid duplicate data. No untagged FETCH SHOULD be sent if a message joins the search results only because of a flag or annotation change.

The motivation is mobile clients that want mail pushed only when it matches a SEARCH pattern.
sections.eli5: You can ask to be told only about letters that match something you care about, like letters from your boss, and the clerk includes the details you asked for.

sections.title: Risks and Registrations
sections.content:
The security section is mostly about self-inflicted harm. It is easy for a client to deny itself service: asking for all events on all mailboxes may work on a small server, but on a big one it can swamp the client's network connection or processing capability, and can even degrade service for other clients.

Server authors should expect that a client may issue requests and not read the responses. The TCP window can then fill, and a careless server might block. The extension magnifies this existing IMAP problem.

Pushing new messages immediately also makes it wholly impractical to delete sensitive messages with programs like imapfilter. The RFC recommends Sieve (RFC 5228) or similar instead.

For IANA, NOTIFY was added to the list of IMAP extensions, and the OLDNAME extended data item was registered in the LIST-EXTENDED registry.
sections.eli5: If you ask to hear about everything everywhere, you will be buried in notes. Asking carefully keeps things calm for you and for the clerk.
